claims.claim: The problem has an exact objective-preserving Local Neighborhood Test Cover reformulation: after adjoining a dummy element, admissible tests are nonempty subsets of a host's closed neighborhood, and every pair of elements must be separated. Approximation and inapproximability results transfer in both directions without loss.
claims.evidence: For the same compact host-graph input, map each bug hosted at z and monitoring M⊆N[z] to test (z,M). A vertex's test-incidence vector is exactly its bug signature, while the dummy has the zero vector. Separation from the dummy is therefore equivalent to signature nonemptiness, and separation of two vertices is equivalent to distinct signatures. The converse map hosts one bug per selected test. Empty or duplicate tests are removable, so the maps preserve objective value and approximation ratios exactly; the identity input transformation also transfers hardness.
claims.witness: The mutually inverse maps (bug z,M)↔(local test z,M), with dummy signature ∅, preserve every solution's cardinality.
claims.search_method: Direct proof from the sealed source model and draft; no web. Exhaustive independent comparison of the two optima on all 75 labeled graphs of orders 1–4.

claims.claim: Fixed-placement feasibility has an exact matching characterization, yielding an XP exact algorithm parameterized by the number k of bugs.
claims.evidence: With hosts fixed, vertex v may receive exactly the nonempty subsets of its audible bug set A(v). Thus distinct feasible signatures are precisely a matching saturating the vertex side of the stated bipartite graph. Conversely, a saturating matching defines legal monitored sets bug-by-bug. Enumerating all host multisets of sizes at most k and solving these matchings takes n^{k+O(1)} time, including the 2^k signature side, and decides OPT≤k.
claims.witness: The checker independently enumerates host multisets and performs augmenting-path matching over all nonzero submasks of each A(v).
claims.search_method: Direct two-way characterization and runtime count, followed by exact host-multiset enumeration; no web.

claims.claim: Regional information bound: for every X⊆V, at least ceil(log2(|X|+1)) bugs must be hosted in N[X]. Moreover, the optimum is additive over connected components.
claims.evidence: Every bug appearing in a signature of x∈X has its host in N[x]⊆N[X]. If h bugs are hosted there, X has at most 2^h−1 distinct nonempty signatures, proving h≥ceil(log2(|X|+1)). Restriction of any solution to a component remains a solution there. Conversely, component solutions use disjoint bug identities, so their nonempty signatures cannot collide across components; hence the optima add exactly.
claims.witness: The checker exhaustively confirmed component additivity for every labeled graph through order four and explicitly verified the disjoint regional neighborhoods used later.
claims.search_method: Direct counting and two-way component decomposition; no web.

claims.claim: If every connected component C has a universal safe house, then OPT is exactly sum_C ceil(log2(|C|+1)), computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Applying claim 2 with X=C gives the lower bound ceil(log2(|C|+1)). If u is universal, that many bugs hosted at u are audible throughout C, allowing |C| arbitrary distinct nonempty signatures. This attains the bound, and component additivity gives the sum. Components and universal vertices are identifiable in polynomial time.
claims.witness: Exhaustive small-graph checks compared the formula against independently enumerated optima whenever every component had a universal vertex.
claims.search_method: Direct lower-bound/construction proof plus exhaustive exact checks; no web.

claims.claim: Incidence-capacity lower bound: if rho=max_v |N[v]| and a solution has k bugs, then L(n,k)≤k rho, where L(n,k) is the minimum total cardinality of n distinct nonempty subsets of a k-element set.
claims.evidence: Double counting gives ∑_v|S(v)|=∑_b|M(b)|. Every monitored set M(b) lies in the closed neighborhood of its host and therefore has size at most rho, so the sum is at most k rho. Because the n signatures are distinct and nonempty, their total size is at least L(n,k). Combining these inequalities proves the claim.
claims.witness: For every independently optimized labeled graph through order four, the checker calculated L(n,k), total signature incidence, and k rho and verified L(n,k)≤∑|S(v)|≤k rho.
claims.search_method: Direct incidence double count plus exact finite checks; no web.

claims.claim: The problem is exactly solvable on interval graphs of maximum degree at most two. For every connected component C of order n, OPT(C)=floor(n/2)+1; componentwise summation gives the general answer.
claims.evidence: A connected graph of maximum degree two is a path or cycle. Interval graphs have no induced cycles of length at least four, leaving paths and K3. For P_n, L(n,k)≥2n−k and rho≤3 imply k≥ceil(n/2). When n=2t, equality k=t would force every bug to occupy an internal vertex and monitor all three neighbors, every singleton signature to occur, and all remaining signatures to be pairs. Cohosting then precludes the required singleton, while adjacent hosts give duplicate two-bug signatures. Thus t distinct nonadjacent internal hosts would be required, but P_{2t} has at most t−1. Hence k≥t+1. Bugs on odd vertices give the matching construction for odd paths; adding a bug at the final vertex gives it for even paths. K3 has optimum two.
claims.witness: Independent placement enumeration verified the formula for P1 through P12 and for K3.
claims.search_method: Complete classification, incidence equality-case analysis, explicit constructions, and exact enumeration; no web.

claims.claim: Running the source greedy algorithm in both timeline directions and taking the better result is not exact, even on a connected symmetric instance: both runs use seven bugs while OPT=6.
claims.evidence: Exact simulation reproduced forward additions (1,2),(2,3),(4,6),(6,7),(9,11),(11,13),(13,13). The interval family is invariant under reflection x↦15−x, and exact reverse simulation also used seven bugs. The stated six-bug code certificate is legal and injective. For X={L1,…,L4}, N[X]={L1,…,L6}, requiring three hosted bugs; the reflected four-vertex region independently requires three in a disjoint six-vertex neighborhood. Thus OPT≥6, while the certificate gives OPT≤6.
claims.witness: The checker reports SYMMETRIC_INSTANCE 7 7 6 and also exhaustively rejects every placement with fewer than six bugs.
claims.search_method: Exact rational interval intersections, literal source-order simulation, regional lower bounds, certificate validation, and exhaustive matching search; no web.

claims.claim: There is a connected ten-interval instance on which the source greedy algorithm uses five bugs in each timeline direction while OPT=4; thus the bidirectional variant has approximation ratio at least 5/4.
claims.evidence: The ten stated intervals form one connected component and occur in the asserted forward and reverse orders. Bugs at I2,I5,I9,I9 realize the ten stated masks 1,3,2,14,5,10,12,8,6,4; each used bug is audible at its assigned vertex, and all masks are nonzero and distinct. Since 2^3−1<10, OPT=4. Exact execution reproduced the forward pattern F,F,T,F,T,T,F,T,T,F with five additions and the reverse pattern F,F,T,F,T,T,T,F,T,F with five additions. The draft's Hall deficits and all intervening matching certificates were independently validated.
claims.witness: The checker reports TEN_INTERVAL_INSTANCE 5 5 4 and verifies every listed Hall-union cardinality and mask certificate.
claims.search_method: Exact integer interval geometry, literal greedy simulation, Hall/matching verification, certificate checking, and exhaustive rejection of all three-bug placements; no web.

claims.claim: For every t≥1 there is an interval instance with OPT=4t on which both timeline directions use 5t bugs; consequently 5/4 is an asymptotic lower bound for the bidirectional greedy approximation ratio.
claims.evidence: Translate t copies far enough apart to create t components. Claim 2 and the verified four-bug certificate give OPT=4t. In either timeline direction, copies are processed consecutively. Bugs from other components are inaudible, and nonempty signatures supported on disjoint bug identities cannot collide, so each copy induces exactly its verified five-addition forward or reverse execution. Both costs are therefore 5t for every t, with ratio 5/4 and unbounded instance size.
claims.witness: The checker constructed separated copies for t=1,2,3 and obtained (forward,reverse,lower bound)=(5t,5t,4t); the component-independence argument proves the quantified extension to every t.
claims.search_method: Symbolic component-factorization proof supplemented by exact simulations of multiple translated copies; no web.

target_evidence: The source target demands either a polynomial-time approximation ratio strictly below two for all interval instances or an appropriate matching inapproximability theorem. The draft explicitly supplies neither and says the general target remains unresolved. Its exact reformulation, XP characterization, special-case formulas, lower bounds, and asymptotic 5/4 obstruction for one bidirectional greedy heuristic are correct and material partial progress, but they do not establish the requested general approximation or hardness result. Therefore PARTIAL is accurate.
